set_title: Passage 1 Stoicism CAT 2022 Slot 1 Verbal Reading Comprehension
question_text: Which one of the following statements, if false, could be seen as contradicting the facts/arguments in the passage?
option_a: In the Stoic view, choosing a reasoned, unemotional response as the first movement is an appropriate response to emotional situations.
option_b: The Greek philosopher Zeno survived into the Roman era until about AD 300.
option_c: Despite practising meditation and cultivating the right attitude, emotions cannot ever be controlled.
option_d: In the Epicurean view, indulging in simple pleasures is not desirable.
correct_answer: In the Epicurean view, indulging in simple pleasures is not desirable.
solution: Option 4. Consider the following lines: “The Epicureans, first associated with the Greek philosopher Epicurus . . . held a similar view, believing that people should enjoy simple pleasures, such as good conversation, friendship, food, and wine, but not be indulgent in these pursuits and not follow passion for those things that hold no real value like power and money.” Now, if the fourth option is false, it would contradict the views quoted above.

set_title: Passage 2 Critical theory CAT 2022 Slot 1 Verbal Reading Comprehension
question_text: Which one of the following statements best reflects the main argument of the fourth paragraph of the passage?
option_a: Automobiles represent the interest in mobility present in human nature.
option_b: Technological environments privilege certain dimensions of human nature as effectively as laws and customs.
option_c: Technology, laws, and customs are comparable, but dissimilar phenomena.
option_d: Technology, laws, and customs are not unlike each other if considered as institutions.
correct_answer: Technology, laws, and customs are not unlike each other if considered as institutions.
solution: Option 4. The main idea of the fourth paragraph is encapsulated in its opening line: “As an environment, technologies shape their inhabitants. In this respect, they are comparable to laws and customs.” The rest of the paragraph is elaborating upon this point.

set_title: Passage 2 Critical theory CAT 2022 Slot 1 Verbal Reading Comprehension
question_text: Which one of the following statements contradicts the arguments of the passage?
option_a: Marx’s understanding of the capitalist rationalisation of production and Marcuse's understanding of a “project” of “technological rationality” share theoretical inclinations.
option_b: Paradoxically, the capitalist rationalisation of production is a mark of so-called socialist systems as well.
option_c: Masses are organised in patterns set by Foucault’s prisons and Habermas’ public sphere.
option_d: The problems of command over a disempowered and deskilled labour force gave rise to similar patterns of the capitalist rationalisation of production wherever masses were organised.
correct_answer: Masses are organised in patterns set by Foucault’s prisons and Habermas’ public sphere.
solution: Option 3. The reference to Foucault’s prisons or Habermas’s public sphere is an example of ways in which masses are organized. These are not the only ways in which this is done.

set_title: Chinese Passage 3 CAT 2022 Slot 1 Verbal Reading Comprehension
question_text: Which one of the following scenarios is unlikely to follow from the arguments in the passage?
option_a: A 21st century Christian scientist is likely to oppose cloning because of his philosophical orientation.
option_b: A 17th century British painter would have no problem adding personal touches when restoring an ancient Roman painting.
option_c: A 17th century French artist who adhered to a Christian worldview would need to be completely true to the original intent of a painting when restoring it.
option_d: A 20th century Japanese Buddhist monk would value a reconstructed shrine as the original.
correct_answer: A 17th century French artist who adhered to a Christian worldview would need to be completely true to the original intent of a painting when restoring it.
solution: Option: 3. The passage says that the 21st century West is not willing to accept cloning because they believe in and adhere to the idea of not tampering with the original. Option 1 is likely to follow from the passage. Since things were different in the 17th century than what it is today, artists would not mind tampering with the original. Option 2 follows from the passage. Option 3 is opposite to what the passage states. In fact, if 2 follows from the passage, then 3 must also follow from the passage. One might wonder why not 4. The fact that Eastern people do not object to the idea of imitation does not mean that they would not value reconstructed shrine as the original. Only 3 is unlikely to follow, rest all will follow.

set_title: Musicking Passage 4 CAT 2022 Slot 2 Verbal Reading Comprehension
question_text: Based on the passage, which one of the following statements is a valid argument about the emergence of music/musicking?
option_a: Although musicking is not language-like, it shares the quality of being a form of expression.
option_b: All musical work is located in the overlap between linguistic capacity and music production.
option_c: Anyone who can perceive and experience music must be considered capable of musicking.
option_d: 20,000 years ago, human musical capacities were not very different from what they are today.
correct_answer: 20,000 years ago, human musical capacities were not very different from what they are today.
solution:
Option: 4. This should be an easy question to answer because the question asks us to pick the valid argument. It means that there is one valid argument and the other three are not. 3 is a valid argument because it is the very theme of the passage. 2 also finds mention in the passage. To prove 2, you just have to look at the options and the right answers of the preceding two questions. 1 also is true as per the passage. 4 is also correct.
You must be wondering, then, why option 4 is the right answer if all the other choices are factually correct. For this you have to read the question carefully. It asks you to pick a choice ‘about the emergence of music/musicking’. Options 1,2, and 3, though correct, have nothing to do with the emergence of musicking. Emergence of musicking has been discussed in the last two paragraphs.
